content.equation:
Ideal Body Weight, Devine Method:
Male: IBW = 50 + [2.3 x (height - 60)]
Female: IBW = 45.5 + [2.3 x (height - 60)]
IBW = ideal body weight in kg
Height measured in inches
For patients <60 inches, default weights of 50 kg for males and 45.5 kg for females are used in this
calculation.
Ideal Body Weight, Robinson Method:
Male: IBW = 52 + [1.9 x (height - 60)]
Female: IBW = 49 + [1.7 x (height - 60)]
IBW = ideal body weight in kg
Height measured in inches
For patients <60 inches, default weights of 52 kg for males and 49 kg for females are used in this calculation.
Adjusted Body Weight:
ABW = IBW + [0.4 x (actual weight - IBW)]
IBW = ideal body weight
notes: This calculation is for adult patients. If a patient's actual weight is less than or equal to their ideal body weight, this calculation will not continue and actual body weight should be used to determine medication doses. Adjusted body weight (sometimes referred to as dosing weight) is a mathematical process often used to dose medications (especially hydrophilic drugs) dosed by weight when a person's actual weight is >130% of their ideal body weight. Drug pharmacokinetics in obese patients are very complex and there is often limited data on use in obese patients. About 30% of adipose tissue is water. Since drug pharmacokinetics in obese patients are so variable, careful monitoring of endpoints, toxicity, response, and serum drug levels is essential. Ideal body weight is a mathematical process of determining a person's 'ideal' weight based on their height and gender. The formulas take into consideration population averages for individuals of similar body types. The Devine method is the most commonly used formula for calculating ideal body weight.
conditional_notes: Caution actual weight is less than ideal, do not use adjusted body weight.
